recentItems.title: 1,500 km deep into Russia without GPS: Ukraine and Germany ASTONISH with cutting-edge drones
recentItems.description:
Ukrainian strike drones are reaching a whole new level: Germany is launching serial production of thousands of systems built upon Ukrainian developments and combat experience. Sat-X is designed to strike targets near the frontline and can operate under heavy GPS jamming, while the heavier Anubis boasts a reported range of up to 1,500 km. German industrial capacity gives Ukraine the ability to scale production in a safer environment. In parallel, Berlin is sharpening its focus on Russian hybrid threats following an incident at the Leipzig airport. How this cooperation changes the game — in this report.

recentItems.description:

Against this backdrop, Russians are increasingly searching for information on mobilization and leaving the country. At the same time, Germany has accused Moscow of involvement in a drone incident at Leipzig Airport and announced new restrictions. NATO and the EU backed Berlin, stating their readiness to step up pressure on Russia.

recentItems.title: They covered the port AND burned their own "Pantsir": FIASCO of Russian air defense in Sochi
recentItems.description:
Ukraine continues to strike Russia's strategic assets, targeting the Port of Sochi, major oil refineries, military warehouses, and Russian aviation. Moscow airports suspend operations once again, as Kyiv warns of hazards in Russian airspace. Meanwhile, the EU prepares billions of euros for Patriot systems and air defense assets, while Germany will deliver IRIS-T missiles and thousands of drones to Ukraine. Also featured: an incident in Leipzig linked to Russia by German authorities, prompting Berlin and the EU to ramp up sanctions and diplomatic pressure on Moscow.
